text: For isosceles triangles, the angles at the base are equal to one another, and if the equal sides are produced then the angles under the base will be equal to one another. Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle having the side $AB$ equal to the side $AC$, and let the straight-lines $BD$ and $CE$ have been produced in a straight-line with $AB$ and $AC$ (respectively) [Post.~2]. I say that the angle $ABC$ is equal to $ACB$, and (angle) $CBD$  to $BCE$.
For let the point $F$ have been taken at random on  $BD$,
and let $AG$ have been cut off from the greater $AE$, equal to the lesser $AF$ [Prop.~1.3].
Also, let the straight-lines $FC$ and $GB$ have been joined [Post.~1].
In fact, since $AF$ is equal to $AG$, and $AB$ to $AC$, the two (straight-lines) $FA$, $AC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $GA$, $AB$, respectively.
assertion: the two straight-lines FA, AC equal the two straight-lines GA, AB, respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: two (straight-lines) $FA$, $AC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $GA$, $AB$, respectively

text: They also encompass a common angle, $FAG$.
assertion: the angle FAG is common to both triangles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: They also encompass a common angle, $FAG$

text: Thus, the base $FC$ is equal to the base $GB$,
assertion: base FC equals base GB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: base $FC$ is equal to the base $GB$

text: and the triangle $AFC$ will be equal to the triangle $AGB$,
assertion: triangle AFC equals triangle AGB (congruent)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: triangle $AFC$ will be equal to the triangle $AGB$

text: and the remaining angles subtendend by the equal sides will be equal to the corresponding  remaining angles [Prop.~1.4].
assertion: the remaining angles subtended by the equal sides equal the corresponding remaining angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: remaining angles subtendend by the equal sides will be equal to the corresponding  remaining angles

text: (That is) $ACF$ to $ABG$,
assertion: angle ACF equals angle ABG

text: and $AFC$ to $AGB$.
assertion: angle AFC equals angle AGB

text: And since the whole of $AF$ is equal to the whole of $AG$, within which $AB$ is equal to $AC$, the remainder $BF$ is thus equal to the remainder $CG$ [C.N.~3].
assertion: the remainder BF equals the remainder CG

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the whole of $AF$ is equal to the whole of $AG$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: remainder $BF$ is thus equal to the remainder $CG$

text: But $FC$ was also shown (to be) equal to $GB$.
assertion: FC equals GB (recalled)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $FC$ was also shown (to be) equal to $GB$

text: So the two (straight-lines) $BF$, $FC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $CG$, $GB$, respectively,
assertion: the two straight-lines BF, FC equal the two straight-lines CG, GB, respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: two (straight-lines) $BF$, $FC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $CG$, $GB$, respectively

text: and the angle $BFC$ (is) equal to the angle $CGB$,
assertion: angle BFC equals angle CGB

text: and the base $BC$ is common to them.
assertion: base BC is common to both triangles

text: Thus, the triangle $BFC$ will be equal to the triangle $CGB$,
assertion: triangle BFC equals triangle CGB (congruent)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: triangle $BFC$ will be equal to the triangle $CGB$

text: and the remaining angles subtended by the equal sides will be equal to the corresponding remaining angles [Prop.~1.4].
assertion: the remaining angles subtended by the equal sides equal the corresponding remaining angles

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: remaining angles subtended by the equal sides will be equal to the corresponding remaining angles

text: Thus, $FBC$ is equal to $GCB$,
assertion: angle FBC equals angle GCB

text: and $BCF$ to $CBG$.
assertion: angle BCF equals angle CBG

text: Therefore, since the whole angle $ABG$ was shown (to be) equal to the whole angle $ACF$, within which $CBG$ is equal to $BCF$, the remainder $ABC$ is thus equal to the remainder $ACB$ [C.N.~3].
assertion: the remainder angle ABC equals the remainder angle ACB

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the whole angle $ABG$ was shown (to be) equal to the whole angle $ACF$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: remainder $ABC$ is thus equal to the remainder $ACB$

text: And they are at the base of triangle $ABC$.
assertion: angles ABC and ACB are at the base of triangle ABC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: And they are at the base of triangle $ABC$

text: And $FBC$ was also shown (to be) equal to $GCB$.
assertion: angle FBC equals angle GCB (recalled)

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $FBC$ was also shown (to be) equal to $GCB$

text: And they are under the base.
assertion: angles FBC and GCB (that is, CBD and BCE) are under the base

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: And they are under the base

text: Thus, for isosceles triangles, the angles at the base are equal to one another, and if the equal sides are produced then the angles under the base will be equal to one another. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
